Sara —

Thanks for the worksheet — attaching our initial ratecard PDF (redwood_ratecard_v1.pdf) and a concise crosswalk below. I'll follow up with a short commercial proposal once we confirm the preferred deployment path.

Executive summary (quick):
- Hosted (baseline): pay-as-you-go. Per-token/embedding economics are higher at low volume but no infra ops. Example: generation ~ $0.0035/token (~$3.50 per 1k tokens) for our standard gen SKU; embeddings ~ $0.0012/vector. Operational benefits: instant scale, platform-managed KV caching and autoscaling.
- Reserved / Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit). Typical committed pool for the profile you shared (15M gen tokens / 500k embeddings) would be a 4-GPU small pool; list price example ~$28k/month reserved for predictable throughput. Effective unit cost often 25–40% lower vs hosted at committed volumes because you amortize instance cost and reduce per-request overheads.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): one-time deployment + license + ongoing support. Example structure: one-time platform delivery & onboarding $300k, annual platform fee $12k/month, plus runbook/SRE support tiers. Private yields lowest marginal token cost but highest upfront/ops responsibility.

Key cost drivers: model family (larger LLMs drive token CPU/GPU time), QAT/quantization (4-bit optimized models reduce inference time substantially), caching hit rate (prefix reuse), and concurrency shaping (batching vs low-latency single token requests).

Attached: redwood_ratecard_v1.pdf (high-level rates) — I'll loop in Priyom and Rafael to propose a commercial structure we can present to procurement.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Greenwave prefers a fully managed hosted POC or wants a reserved pool for predictable latency.
2) If reserved/private: recommend a 12-month commit to unlock deeper discounts (we can model 15–30% discounts depending on commitment).

Thanks — happy to review on a call.

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_ratecard_v1.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Fwd: Rate card and environment options — proposed commercial framework

Team —

Draft proposal to answer Greenwave's clarifications and provide a commercial path:

1) Reserved pool billing: base reserved fee covers committed capacity and 95% of expected throughput. Bursts are billed at a lower overlay rate (hosted overlay minus 10%). Example: $28k/month committed + $0.0020/token for burst above commit. This keeps predictable monthly cost while allowing headroom.

2) Private delivery: $300k one-time includes platform install, basic integration with customer KMS (ours supports common KMS providers; HSM/airgap add-ons priced separately), and 4 weeks of on-site validation for a standard rack. Estimated lead time 6–8 weeks after PO. Annual platform fee $12k/month for the control plane license; optional SRE support tiers (Silver/Gold/Platinum) priced separately.

3) Quantization assumptions: our baseline numbers assume mixed precision production kernels (8-bit where available). Using 4-bit kernel-optimized models typically reduces inference cost by ~25–45% depending on model size and sequence length. We'll include a line-item sensitivity table in the formal pricing deck.

4) Discounts and commitment: recommend the following table for negotiation:
- 12-month hosted commit (consumption floor) => 10–15% discount on hosted list
- 12-month reserved commit => 20% off list reserved monthly fee (scale bands at 50k/150k/500k token tiers)
- 24-month private license => 15% reduction on one-time delivery fees and 5% off annual fee

I've added a draft SOW for internal review (SOW-draft.docx). Rafael, Marissa: can you sanity-check the numbers and confirm whether the reserved/burst overlay math looks good? Laura: once we align I'll send to Sara + procurement and propose a mid-week call.

— Priyom
